title: Navigating Banner: Essentials for Research Administration — eTraining Module
content:
Navigating Banner: Essentials for Research Administration

Hello Morgan State University Faculty & Staff, Ellucian Banner serves as Morgan State University's Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software. In this module, we will review key pages and processes within Banner necessary for successful research administration support. Topics include how to review award budget and expense activity, how to perform budget and cost transfers, how to query award details by PI and department, how to close encumbrances, and more. Please note that the processes detailed in this module are specific to grant-funded activities. Some of the information may also be relevant to state-funded actions; however, policy and procedural differences may apply. We strive to continuously review these lessons to provide up-to-date guidance on Morgan’s sponsored project processes. For questions related to the activities covered in this module that are not addressed in the module content, please contact the ORA Training and Communications Coordinator: Mr. Ryan Mobley, CRA, CFRA, CPRA Email: ryan.mobley@morgan.edu Phone: 443-885-4771 Thank you, ORA Training Team

Self-paced ORA eTraining module. Source: https://share.articulate.com/P5hdpOIVrXhCKX63DYkkA

A PI's Banner access should be request by their school's Budget Officer. Once access is established, PIs may submit finance access Workflow requests for grant-funded employees on an as-needed basis.

FOAPAL: Banner Grant Codes
heading
WHITE
ACCENT
image
When dealing with budgets you will likely come across the acronym FOAPAL. This refers to a string of codes setup by the Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) team that is unique to a specific budget. FOAPAL stands for:
impact
LIGHT
DEFAULT
interactive
Fund
A project's fund is a 5-digit code unique to a specific project. Many forms will ask for both a project's index and fund number.
Organization Code
Each group on campus (School of Social Work, GESTAR, etc) has a unique organization code that "houses" a project budget. Typically, budgets under each org code are under the purview of the school's Budget Officer.
Account
Budgets are broken down in Banner into pool levels (noted by 2-digit pool level codes). Each pool level has various 5-digit account codes which impact the corresponding budget. For example, your project's supply pool (09) may have office supply expenses (09021) charged against it.
Program
This helps identify the funding source. For the vast majority of grants on campus the program code will always be 25.
Activity
Many project budgets will not utilize the activity code, but it is used to identify special activity such as cost share on grants. Please review our cost share module for more information on cost share activity codes.
Location
This is typically not used on grants, but may be utilized for fixed assets.

Native Banner: FGIBDST Page
Make your way to the Native Banner landing page, type the page code FGIBDST in the search bar, and select "Organization Budget Status".
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/LpUAtnWru529tP--.png
Enter Budget Details
At the top of the FGIBDST page you will need to update a few fields: Budget Index: 6-digit code assigned by RFA when the project arrives at Morgan. uncheck the "Include Revenue" box Enter your Fiscal Year For example, FY24 would cover July 1st, 2023 through June 30th, 2024. The remaining necessary fields will auto populate. After entering the information above click on "Go" button in the top right of the screen.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/UNEiRvPrblWfwHP8.jpg
Budget View Details
The important fields in the budget view are: Account : Reflects the Banner charge code associated with a given transaction. Budgets are broken down into pool levels (2-digit levels) with 5-digit account codes impacting the associated budget level. Title : A description of the budget or charge code. Adjusted Budget : Available total budget for the given fiscal year. YTD Activity : Transactions that have impacted your budget. Some charges may take time to reflect as YTD activity such as travel reimbursements submitted and monthly p-card transactions. Commitments : Funds held, but not spent. Examples may include travel authorizations and requisitions. Available Balance : Reflects the combined direct and indirect costs budget allocation remaining on the project. Positive figures reflect budget pools and the negative figures are project costs. It is important to remember that you need to reduce the remaining balance of your project's indirect cost pool (Pool 15) from your total available budget when calculating your remaining direct costs budget.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/7z6H5opBFsYqVutN.png
Identify Specific Transaction Details (Part 1)
Under FGIBDST you can lookup specific transactions by account number. To do so, first click on the YTD Activity charge total for the account code you need more details on. With the cost highlighted, click on the "Related" tab in the upper right corner of the screen.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/BPR99azBwcnsWv50.jpg
Identify Specific Transaction Details (Part 2)
Select "Transaction Detail Information".
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/vQyQL-4Zy7uksILs.jpg
Identify Specific Transaction Details (Part 3)
This view shows each activity that has impacted the chosen account. This will include fund commitments, past charges, invoices processed, etc. Below is a brief explanation of some of the information in this view: Field: This column helps identify whether a transaction/entry is an expense or an encumbrance. "YTD" identifies expenses that have hit your budget. "ENC" notes funds that are encumbered/held, but not yet spent. Type: These help further identify how an expense was paid out. A few common ones are "IPNI" for p-card expenses, "INEI" for payments processed through accounts payable (travel reimbursements, vendor payments, etc), and "XJ16" for flights booked through Globetrotter.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/sMy5qevoe7lP9sQj.jpg
Organization Encumbrances (Part 1)
The FGIBDST view provides quick access to a complete list of open encumbrances/commitments on your project. This is especially helpful to review monthly/quarterly and verify invoices have been processed, reimbursements are getting to your travelers, and more.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/n0XGVvCMLWb4_Me3.jpg
Organization Encumbrances (Part 2)
This view will list each project encumbrance and its available encumbered balance.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/luE-VTqvvxnXvPmb.jpg
Exporting Data
You may need the data in Banner presented to you in an excel sheet so you can more easily share budget information with project key personnel or budget support staff. Click on "Tools" in the top right then select "Export" from the dropdown menu.

Native Banner: FGIENCD Page
Make your way to the Native Banner landing page, type the page code FGIENCD in the search bar, and select "Detail Encumbrance Activity".
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/cyAs9K7qoPg0Ke0u.png
Enter Document Number
You can review a variety of encumbrances using the FGIENCD view. Some of these may include: Travel Forms (TLs) : These will start with "TL" followed by a 5-digit reference number. Requisition (REQ) : These will start with an "R" followed by a 7-digit reference number. Purchase Order (PO) : These will start with a "P" followed by a 7-digit reference number. Enter your document number and click on the "Go" button in the upper right corner of the screen.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/BhSE6y8kRS67XlCy.jpg
FGIENCD View Detail
The encumbrance detail view contains a few key fields: Balance Details Encumbrance : Total funds held. Liquidation : Total charges. Balance : Remaining balance. Transaction Activity Transaction Date : Date the transaction impacted your budget at MSU. This will be the date that MSU Accounts Payable processes listed invoices. The vendor will not receive payment for roughly 3 weeks after this date. Type : This identifies the transaction type. Some examples include a purchase order assignment (PORD), a processed invoice (XBD1), fiscal year rollover (E090), etc. Document Code : reference code for a specific action. What happens if you didn't initially budget for an expense in your approved budget outlined in your Notice of Award (NOA)? There may be times when the needs of your project require funds to move from one budget category to another. This is where the Budget Transfer process comes in.

divider

Restrictions on Budget Transfers
Before submitting a budget transfer request the initiator should consider the factors below.
impact
interactive
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/rpD2n5mExbB0aEX_.jpg
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/-CxQb_EbELHyQ3DN.jpg
Sufficient Funds in Pool Level
This may seem obvious, but there must be sufficient funds in the Banner pool level from which you plan to transfer funds. Without enough money the transfer will not be processed.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/P1pwEDj3M6DX_9yH.jpg
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/nQCdEEZQwE6yOI5T.jpg
Allowability
Budget transfers cannot occur if the reason for the transfer is not allowable under the terms of the project award. A common example is equipment. Many projects specifically restrict spending project funds on equipment. If this is the case, a budget transfer will not be approved to move funds to the equipment pool level. Transfer requests should only involve one index per request. Transfers between multiple indexes/projects is not allowable. Budget transfers should not create new budget categories. For example, you should not transfer funds out of supplies to create a new travel budget without prior written sponsor approval.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/Zqa2OVMIKB0p3zQP.jpg
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/rtmS9MFVvHonsp_6.jpg
Change of Project Scope
A budget transfer cannot be processed if doing so would substantially alter the design and scope of the project. If a change in scope would result from the budget transfer it is the PI's responsibility to contact their Program Officer for written authorization to move the funds.
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/5IZ4S8hJxiDQpfV6.jpg
rise/courses/a3KxqjvK34Th8rPzu-8KNaVhQHi3pfBC/ua1hBfu92-omsT4J.jpg
Pool Level & Percentage Change Restrictions
Many sponsors have limitations on how much funding can be moved between the pool levels outlined in the project Notice of Award. For example, NIH-sponsored projects typically limit budget transfers to no more than 25% of the total project budget. Additionally, several Banner pool levels have their own specific restrictions. Some examples include the following: 01&02 (Salaries) : Key Personnel, PIs and CO-PIs, cannot move more than 25% of their proposed salary/effort without approval from the Program Officer. 11 (Equipment) : If your NOA/FOA explicitly restricts equipment purchases then funds cannot be transferred into the 11 Banner pool level. 12 (Participant Support) : Moving funds out of pool level 12 requires written authorization from the project's Program Officer. 15 (Indirect Cost, IDC) : Funds cannot be transferred out of pool level 15 and added to a direct cost pool level such as 09 (Supplies) unless the transfer in/out of pool level 15 is to compensate for funds moving from an IDC-assessed pool level to a non-assessed one. For example, let's say you have a $2,000,000 project with $100,000 in your equipment pool level. Now your project needs have changed and you can use a less-expensive piece of equipment ($50,000) to perform the work without impacting your project scope. To move the excess equipment funds to your travel pool (04) the $50,000 would need to be split between 04 and 15 to account for the increased IDC capture ($32,679 to 04 & $17,321 to 15 based on a 53% IDC rate). IDC is not assessed on activities under pool level 12 (Participant Support), pool level 11 (Equipment), or subawards after IDC is captured on the first 25k of the subaward. Current IDC rates can be found here .

Add Accounting #1

What happens if a charge is posted to the wrong place? For example, you may miss the p-card reallocation deadline in Banner, or a requisition may be submitted using the wrong index. In these situations, the correction is made through a cost transfer . A Cost transfer allows a PI or project admin to request that an expense be moved from one funding source or budget category to another, such as a different index or account.
text aside

Process: Cost Transfer Request
interactive
Step #1
Collect Your Documentation
To request a cost transfer you will need to collect a few pieces of supporting documentation to include the following: Completed Cost Transfer Form (blank copy and example forms below) Invoice/Receipt of Expense (if applicable) If the request is to move multiple P-card expenses that were misallocated then the associated approved p-card log can be submitted without including multiple receipts. If the request is due to missing the reallocation deadline for reconciling your p-card in Banner please contact the p-card office directly at pcardreconciliation@morgan.edu . Banner Budget Screenshots One showing the location of the expense to be moved and another showing the budget availability of where the expense will be moved to. Prepared Justification Cost transfer requests submitted more than 90 days after the original transaction date require additional justification. The request must explain why the transfer is necessary, why it was not completed timely, and what internal control improvements will be implemented to prevent similar late transfers in the future. Because late cost transfers are considered a high audit risk, they should be rare and well-documented.
Step #2
Contact Your RFA Grant Accountant
With the cost transfer form and supporting documents in hand you need to contact your Restricted Funds (RFA) Grant Accountant. If you do not know your RFA accountant please contact the RFA Director, Mr. Jeffrey Copeland (jeffrey.copeland@morgan.edu). The RFA team will review the charge(s) to ensure they are being moved to the correct budget and pool level. Once RFA has the completed cost transfer form and supporting documentation, and has reviewed them for accuracy, they will complete the cost transfer via journal entry.

A labor redistribution is the process of moving salary and associated fringe benefit expenses from one funding source to another after payroll has already posted. In sponsored projects, labor redistributions commonly occur in situations such as: Pre-award spending (when authorized), where payroll expenses must temporarily post to a non-sponsored index until the official award/index is established. Incorrect or incomplete effort assignments during the contracting or EPAF documentation process. Corrections needed to align payroll charges with actual work performed.

At MSU, labor redistributions are processed through use of the Labor/Payroll Redistribution Form . The form must include sufficient justification for the requested adjustment and is routed for review, approval, and processing by Morgan's RFA (rfa@morgan.edu) team.
ACCENT
2026-05-13T18:36:20.921Z
interactive
Requester Information
Fill the requested fields. Email should be the individual's MSU email address. Extension should be their MSU phone extension.
MSU ID and Employee Name
For the labor that needs to be reallocated, please include the employee's MSU ID and Name.
Pay Number
Pay numbers reference the Contractual/Regular Payroll Schedules (found here ) available via MSU's Payroll department.
Pay ID
This refers to the contract type for the labor that needs to be moved. B1 refers to Regular (salaried) positions while B2 refers to Contractual positions.
Year
Enter the fiscal year in which the labor activity was originally posted.
"From" Section
Here you need to supply the grant codes for the budget labor needs to be moved out of. Index is the 6-digit budget code assigned to the project. Fund is the 5-digit budget code assigned to the project. Activity Code likely will only be used in the case of cost share labor.
"To" Section
Like the "From" section of this form. Here you need to supply the grant codes for the budget labor needs to be moved into. Index is the 6-digit budget code assigned to the project. Fund is the 5-digit budget code assigned to the project. Activity Code likely will only be used in the case of cost share labor.
Salary Amount
Enter the amount for salary only (no fringe). Associated fringe will automatically be moved along with their related salary costs.
Why Transfer?
You will need to identify the reason for the labor redistribution request. Select the best option or enter your justification in the "other" category.

labeledgraphic
2026-05-13T18:21:30.213Z
Allocation of Labor
You need to justify why the labor needs to be moved to the newly identified budget. For example, you might explain that an error was made during the EPAF contracting process and labor was always meant to be allocated to this budget. Or you may explain that work was performed under a contract for Grant A, but the effort was actually for Grant B. As such, labor needs to be properly allocated.
Error Corrected
You need to explain the error that occurred and detail how the error was corrected. For example, you might explain that you provided the corrected index/fund information to Human Resources to update the contract funding.
Internal Controls
This section effectively asks you to identify what internal controls were enacted or revised to ensure this same error does not occur again. Examples may include adding index/fund verification through the project's PI, securing a secondary review from another admin to verify funding accuracy, etc.
DocuSign Submission
This form should be submitted via DocuSign. Please create an envelope and ensure the identified individuals are part of your envelope's approval queue. The RFA section can use the RFA@morgan.edu email address.
